scripts.radio:
Hamjambo and welcome to Kenya on Record, your weekly check-in on public accountability and the rule of law. 

This week, our justice system reached a significant, sobering milestone. The High Court has convicted Paul Mackenzie alongside twenty-eight of his co-accused of murder in connection with the horrific tragedy in Shakahola forest. The court has scheduled sentencing for November.

For months, the nation watched in disbelief as hundreds of bodies—many of them innocent children—were exhumed from shallow graves in Kilifi County, starved to death under the guise of religious devotion. The legal process has been slow, heavy, and painful, but this verdict matters. It reinforces an essential principle: religious freedom does not grant anyone a license to manipulate, exploit, and destroy human life. State institutions and judicial officers had to prove these charges beyond reasonable doubt, and the conviction shows that accountability is possible even in cases of overwhelming scale.

Yet, a conviction alone cannot heal the deep wounds left in those communities, nor does it excuse the administrative blind spots that allowed this crisis to grow unnoticed for so long. As citizens, our duty is to remain vigilant, protect the vulnerable in our midst, and question any group that demands complete isolation from family and society.

Kwa ufupi: Mahakama Kuu imempata Paul Mackenzie na wenzake ishirini na wanane na hatia ya mauaji kuhusiana na vifo vya msitu wa Shakahola, huku hukumu ikipangwa kutolewa mwezi Novemba. Sheria imechukua mkondo wake, lakini wajibu wa kulinda jamii zetu unabaki mikononi mwetu.
scripts.voice_note: Hey everyone, quick accountability update from Kenya on Record. The High Court has officially convicted Paul Mackenzie and twenty-eight co-accused of murder over the Shakahola deaths, with formal sentencing set for November. This verdict doesn't erase the grief or bring back the hundreds who starved to death in that forest, but it is an essential reckoning. Legally, it draws a firm boundary: faith cannot be weaponized as an excuse for abuse, coercion, and murder. Justice is grinding forward through our courts. But beyond the courtroom, the takeaway for all of us is vigilance. When any group isolates your relatives, tells them to stop eating, or demands they cut off society, don't keep quiet. Report it early and look out for one another. Pass this on.
scripts.sms: Usiibiwe: Faith should never demand starvation, secrecy, or cutting off your family. If a religious group isolates its members, speak out and report it early.
scripts.reels: A major turning point in the Shakahola tragedy. The High Court has convicted Paul Mackenzie and twenty-eight co-accused of murder, setting sentencing for this November. While no verdict can restore the hundreds of lives lost to starvation and indoctrination, this ruling sends an unequivocal message: faith cannot shield anyone from criminal accountability. Justice is moving. Let’s stay alert, protect our vulnerable, and never look away.
